proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 20 currently contains only a broad Customer indemnity and no Vendor indemnity, and Section 9.3 already cross-references remedies in Section 20.5 that do not exist. We have added a Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused compromise of Customer Data and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, together with standard indemnification procedure and infringement remedies, and narrowed Customer's indemnity to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

ops.newText: Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) content or materials Customer provides to Vendor for use in the Services, or (b) Customer's breach of Applicable Law.
ops.oldText: Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services.

ops.text: Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services, Deliverables, or Vendor Technology infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of the claim (delay does not excuse the indemnity except to the extent it materially prejudices the defence), permit the indemnifying Party to control the defence with counsel reasonably acceptable to the indemnified Party, and provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense. The indemnified Party may participate with its own counsel at its own cost. The indemnifying Party shall not settle a claim in a way that imposes a non-indemnified obligation or admission on the indemnified Party without its prior written consent.

Vendor's obligation under Section 20.2(a) does not apply to the extent the claim arises from Customer's modification of a Deliverable without Vendor's involvement, combination of the Services with items not supplied or recommended by Vendor where the claim would not have arisen but for the combination, or Vendor's compliance with detailed written specifications supplied by Customer.

If an infringement claim is made or is reasonably likely, Vendor shall, at its expense and at Customer's option, procure the right for Customer to continue using the affected item, or modify or replace it with a functionally equivalent, non-infringing item. If neither remedy is reasonably available, Customer may terminate the affected Services or Deliverables and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees allocable to the terminated items and Fees paid for Deliverables Customer can no longer use. These remedies do not limit Vendor's indemnity under Section 20.2.

quote: 20. INDEMNIFICATION 20.1 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services.
rationale: Section 20 is a one-way, unlimited Customer indemnity ("every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services") with no Vendor indemnity at all — including no IP infringement indemnity, which is the playbook walk-away position. Section 9.3 already assumes infringement remedies "required by Section 20.5", a provision that does not exist, so the indemnity architecture is incomplete. We therefore added a Vendor defence and indemnity covering third-party IP infringement, Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused compromise of Customer Data, and Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, plus standard notice/control/cooperation procedure, customary exclusions and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies in a new Section 20.5 to support Section 9.3, and narrowed Customer's indemnity to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law. Indemnity obligations are already Excluded Claims under Section 21.3, so no super-cap change is needed.

quote: 14.2 Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel. Vendor will execute further documents reasonably needed to confirm ownership.
rationale: Section 14 matches our preferred position. 14.1 confirms Customer owns Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information and independently developed IP, with only a limited processing right to Vendor (and no transfer of rights); 14.2 gives Customer ownership of Deliverables with an express Vendor assignment and personnel assignments; 14.3 leaves Vendor its pre-existing Vendor Technology but applies the perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence in 13.2 to any Vendor Technology embedded in or required to use a Deliverable; 14.4 blocks joint ownership absent a signed instrument and preserves our unrestricted right to use our own feedback. The definitions do not shrink what we own — "Deliverable" (1.4) excludes only Vendor Technology and unaided know-how, and "Vendor Technology" (1.8) expressly excludes Customer Data and pre-existing Customer IP — and 15.1 bars Vendor from selling Customer Data, using it for advertising, combining it with other customers' identifiable data, or training a generally available model on it without our written consent. No assignment of our IP or data to Vendor appears anywhere in the document. No redline needed.

We also removed "without exception" so that the Excluded Claims in Section 21.3 — indemnification, confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement — remain uncapped as that Section contemplates. Our fallback is a mutual cap of twelve months' Fees with those carve-outs preserved.

ops.newText: Except for Excluded Claims, which are not subject to this limitation, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the Fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000.

quote: Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.
rationale: Section 21.1 caps each Party's aggregate liability at Fees "actually paid" in a single month — far below our floor of the greater of 12 months' Fees and USD 1,000,000, and below even the walk-away threshold of six months' fees. "Fees" (Section 1.5) excludes taxes, expenses, credits and one-time implementation charges, so a one-month measure is close to illusory against risks such as a Security Incident (note Vendor carries USD 5,000,000 cyber cover under 18.1). The phrase "without exception" also overrides the Excluded Claims regime in 21.3, pulling indemnities, confidentiality, data-protection, security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement inside the cap. The cap is nominally mutual, so the fix is limited to the basis and restoring the carve-outs: we set the cap at the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000 and reinstate Excluded Claims as uncapped. Sections 21.2–21.4 (mutual consequential-damages exclusion, Excluded Claims definition, payment obligations not "damages") already meet the playbook and are unchanged.

No change-of-control or assignment-triggered Vendor right appears elsewhere (Section 9 termination rights are breach/insolvency-based only). No redline needed.

quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
rationale:
§ 9.4 standing alone meets the preferred position: Customer convenience termination of the Agreement or any Order Form on thirty days' notice, refund of prepaid Fees allocable to the post-termination period, and an express bar on any Vendor convenience right during a committed term. No Vendor convenience right appears anywhere else in the document.

The deviation sits in § 2.1. It binds Customer to a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay minimum "without reduction or termination rights." There is no order-of-precedence or conflict clause in the agreement, so § 2.1 (the more specific commitment) can be read to override § 9.4; at best, even if § 9.4 survives, Customer would terminate yet remain liable for the full unpaid minimum. Either way the convenience right is illusory and the effective exit cost is up to three years of committed spend — far beyond the fallback ceiling of three months' fees, and squarely in walk-away territory (no real Customer convenience right in a multi-year term).

The minimal fix preserves the commercial minimum but carves terminations out of it, so the commitment reduces pro rata and no shortfall or early-termination amount is triggered by an exit under § 9.4. § 9.4 itself needs no edit.
